newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares soar, now awaiting Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares soar, now awaiting Greenspan.

text.p: Belgian shares soared with neighbouring stock markets on Tuesday, though ended below the session's best levels as Wall Street turned easier later in the day and amid renewed caution ahead of a Greenspan speech.

U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is due to give testimony to Congress on Wednesday, and the markets will be listening intently for on any hints on the future direction of U.S. short term interest rates.
The Bel-20 index finished 33.82 points or 1.61 percent stronger at a closing high of 2,138.30, after touching a record 2,147.70 earlier in the session.
A return to flat prices in the bond market after initial gains, and an unchanged dollar in late afternoon after an earlier slight strengthening also began to weigh on shares later in the session.

One dealer said the hefty forward market volume of five billion francs worth of Belgian shares had been boosted by basket trades, apparently related to the current wave of index-linked derivative products being launched by banks.
"It's linked to the derivatives products - it's not normal (trading). It seems some guys have been covering themselves by buying, or maybe some individual was being squeezed," he said.
Of the 20 stocks in the Bel-20 index only one - chemicals and pharmaceuticals firm UCB - ended in the red.
The share finished 0.32 percent lower at 93,700 francs with 2,028 shares traded, though its bid and ask spread at the close was quoted at 93,750/93,900

Other shares to buck the positive trend included Quick Restaurants, down 0.54 percent at 1,840 francs after the company last Friday announced a sharp fall in 1996 profit, and chemicals stock Tessenderlo, down 0.16 percent at 15,875 francs. Tessenderlo said late Monday 1996 net profit fell 17 percent.
